title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a faint scratch page, mostly in pencil with a few blue-ink additions. The neighbouring pages (352, 354) are typed pages of Dennis Sullivan's 'Infinitesimal computations in topology' (Theorem D, iterated integrals, nilpotent towers). Grothendieck's own notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex appear on or among those sheets.

What is legible:
- At the top is a crossed-out formula for a 'ΛC' in terms of iterated exterior powers of Λ^·Φ.
- Next comes a statement that the cycles of a complex C are exterior powers: Z^·(C) = Λ^·(something), later written Λ^·Ψ. The rest of the paragraph is illegible except a question mark.
- The central object is a commutative ladder whose columns are 0 → Z^i → C^i → Z^{i+1} → 0 (inclusion of cycles, then d). The C-column is tensored with Z^j, the target column being Z^{i+j} → C^{i+j} → Z^{i+j+1}:
  - top row: Z^{i+1} ⊗ Z^j → Z^{i+j+1};
  - middle row: σ_ij : C^i ⊗ Z^j → C^{i+j};
  - bottom row: Z^i ⊗ Z^j → Z^{i+j}.

The problem is to extend the multiplication on cycles to a module structure of C over its cycle algebra Z, i.e. to construct σ_ij compatible with d (a Leibniz-type rule d(c·z) = dc·z). The line beginning 'Il ... pour trouver σ_ij et donc ...' reduces this to a Hom (or cohomology) computation involving the map Z^{i+1} ⊗ Z^j → Z^{i+j+1}.

With Z^k ≅ Λ^kΨ, this map becomes the wedge product Λ^{i+1}Ψ ⊗ Λ^jΨ → Λ^{i+j+1}Ψ. The blue ink records a decomposition of the source as Λ^{i+j+1}Ψ ⊕ (a complement, 'quelque chose ... transposition'). That is, a (functorial, possibly up to torsion) splitting of the multiplication map, of Pieri/Cauchy type, which lets one lift.

Context: in the PD (divided-power) de Rham complex of a divided-power polynomial algebra the PD Poincaré lemma gives acyclicity. So the de Rham complex is an extension of its cycle modules, and the cycles of degree ≥1 are generated by exact forms. The page appears to be checking that the multiplicative structure can be reconstructed from the cycles (exterior algebra on Ψ) together with these extension data.
errors: Too little is legible to verify. A splitting Λ^{i+1}Ψ ⊗ Λ^jΨ ≅ Λ^{i+j+1}Ψ ⊕ (complement) holds functorially only rationally, or after inverting small primes. Over Z or in characteristic p the multiplication map need not split functorially, which is exactly the delicate point in a divided-power setting. Whether Grothendieck handled this cannot be read.

ideas.what: Viewing an acyclic complex as an iterated extension 0→Z^i→C^i→Z^{i+1}→0 and seeking a compatible Z-module multiplication σ_ij: C^i⊗Z^j→C^{i+j}
ideas.modern_name: module structure of a dga over its cycles / lifting of products along extensions

ideas.what: Cycles of the (PD) de Rham complex identified with exterior powers Λ^·Ψ, and the wedge product Λ^{i+1}⊗Λ^j→Λ^{i+j+1} split via a functorial decomposition
ideas.modern_name: PD Poincaré lemma; Pieri/Cauchy decomposition of tensor products of exterior powers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Berthelot/Cartier (PD Poincaré lemma); Akin–Buchsbaum–Weyman (characteristic-free Schur functors)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 talk on the divided-power de Rham complex are physically interleaved with Sullivan's preprint on rational homotopy via polynomial de Rham forms. This suggests he viewed the PD de Rham complex as an integral or p-adic analogue of Sullivan's model. Later work (Cenkl–Porter integral forms, Mandell's p-adic homotopy, Toën/Lurie affine stacks) took up such analogues without reference to Grothendieck.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical context for Grothendieck's interest in integral de Rham models of homotopy types. It is only weakly supported by this page itself.

deep.surprise_reason: Faint, routine homological computation: lifting the product along the cycle/boundary extension and splitting exterior-power multiplication. The only point of interest is the juxtaposition with Sullivan's rational homotopy preprint.
transcription_corrections: The ladder has vertical maps: C^i → Z^{i+1} (d) above and Z^i → C^i (inclusion) below. The arrows labelled 'd' on the top and bottom rows look like 'donné' (given), i.e. the given products, not the differential.
The blue-ink lines are Λ^{i+1}Ψ ⊗ Λ^jΨ → Λ^{i+j+1}Ψ with a brace, then '≃ Λ^{i+j}Ψ ⊕ (quelque chose ... d'[?transposition])'. The degree in the first summand is uncertain (i+j or i+j+1).
The '353' at the bottom left is the archive foliation number.
